title: The ‘dad bod’ dilemma
titleZh: 关于“爸爸身材”的新发现
summary:
“爸爸身材”（dad bod）一词常被人们半开玩笑地用来形容部分男性在成为父亲后出现的发福体态。但加州大学欧文分校的一项最新研究显示，这一概念背后的潜在隐患，可能远比人们以往所理解的更为严峻。发表在《当代肥胖报告》上的一篇综述发现，男性在成为父亲前及育儿阶段的健康状况——包括肥胖程度、饮食习惯、压力水平、心理健康和生活方式——都可能影响孩子日后患肥胖症及相关慢性疾病的风险，且这种影响甚至可能在受孕前就已经产生。

来源：University of California；作者：UC Irvine；原文发布时间：2026-06-20 19:59:00

paragraphs.contentEn: The phrase “dad bod” is often used playfully to describe the softer physique some men develop after becoming fathers. But new UC Irvine research suggests that the concept may have more serious implications than previously understood. A review published in Current Obesity Reports finds that a father’s health before and during parenthood — including obesity, diet, stress levels, mental health and lifestyle habits — may influence a child’s risk of obesity and related chronic diseases, even before conception occurs.
paragraphs.contentZh: “爸爸身材”（dad bod）一词常被人们半开玩笑地用来形容部分男性在成为父亲后出现的发福体态。但加州大学欧文分校的一项最新研究显示，这一概念背后的潜在隐患，可能远比人们以往所理解的更为严峻。发表在《当代肥胖报告》上的一篇综述发现，男性在成为父亲前及育儿阶段的健康状况——包括肥胖程度、饮食习惯、压力水平、心理健康和生活方式——都可能影响孩子日后患肥胖症及相关慢性疾病的风险，且这种影响甚至可能在受孕前就已经产生。

paragraphs.contentEn: The findings challenge the long-standing focus on maternal health as the primary driver of childhood obesity risk and point to fathers as important contributors to children’s lifelong well-being. Matthew Landry, assistant professor of population health & disease prevention in the UC Irvine Joe C. Wen School of Population & Public Health and corresponding author of the study, says fathers have a larger role in children’s health than many people realize. “We found that fathers’ health as an important contributor to children’s health through biological, behavioral and environmental pathways,” said Matthew Landry, a registered dietitian nutritionist.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这一研究结果对长期以来将母亲健康视为儿童肥胖风险主导因素的传统观念提出了挑战，同时也表明父亲同样是影响子女终身健康的重要一环。该研究通讯作者、加州大学欧文分校Joe C. Wen人口与公共卫生学院人口健康与疾病预防系助理教授马修·兰德里表示，父亲对孩子健康的影响远比许多人认识到的更大。兼具注册营养师身份的兰德里说：“我们的研究发现，通过生物学、行为习惯和环境等多种途径，父亲的健康状况在孩子的健康发展中扮演着重要角色。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The review examined evidence showing that obesity may affect sperm quality and alter epigenetic markers — biological signals that help regulate how genes function during early development. Researchers believe these changes may influence a child’s metabolism, appetite regulation and long-term disease risk. The findings add another layer to scientists’ understanding of obesity, which is increasingly viewed as a condition shaped by genetics, biology, environment and behavior rather than personal choices alone.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这篇综述梳理了相关证据，表明肥胖可能影响精子质量，并改变表观遗传标记——即在早期发育阶段参与调控基因表达的生物学信号。研究人员认为，这些变化或将影响孩子的新陈代谢、食欲调节能力以及长期患病风险。这一发现为科学界对肥胖的认知增添了新的维度，如今，肥胖正日益被视为一种由遗传、生物学机制、环境及行为习惯共同作用所致的复杂病症，而非单纯归咎于个人选择。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Obesity is not simply the result of individual choices,” Landry said. “This work highlights that obesity risk is 40 to 70 percent heritable and can be passed across generations through complex biological and environmental influences.” While the review highlights potential risks, it also offers encouraging news. Researchers found evidence suggesting that some obesity-related changes in sperm may be reversible. Weight-loss interventions, including healthier lifestyle habits and bariatric surgery, have been associated with improvements in sperm health and favorable changes in obesity-linked epigenetic patterns.
paragraphs.contentZh: 兰德里表示：“肥胖绝非仅仅是个人选择的结果。这项研究表明，40%至70%的肥胖风险与遗传因素有关，且这种风险还可能通过复杂的生物学和环境因素在代际间传递。”不过，这篇综述在提示潜在风险的同时，也释放了一些积极信号。研究人员发现，有证据表明，肥胖引发的某些精子变化或许是可逆的。减重干预措施——包括养成更健康的生活方式以及接受减重手术——已被证实有助于改善精子的健康状况，并能促使与肥胖相关的表观遗传模式发生良性转变。

paragraphs.contentEn: Those findings suggest that prospective fathers may have opportunities to improve not only their own health but also the health prospects of future children. The study arrives at a time when obesity remains a growing public health challenge. According to estimates cited by the researchers, more than 250 million people in the United States could be overweight or obese by 2050. The influence of fathers extends beyond biology. The study found that fathers play a significant role in establishing family routines that affect children’s eating habits and physical activity levels. Fathers’ dietary choices, exercise patterns and parenting approaches are closely linked to children’s health behaviors and obesity risk.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这些发现表明，准备成为父亲的男性不仅有机会改善自身健康，也可能为未来孩子创造更好的健康条件。这项研究发布之际，肥胖仍是一个日益严峻的公共卫生问题。研究人员援引的预测数据显示，到2050年，美国超重或肥胖人口可能超过2.5亿。父亲对孩子的影响并不局限于生物学层面。研究发现，在建立影响孩子的饮食习惯和身体活动水平的家庭生活惯例方面，父亲扮演着关键角色。父亲的饮食习惯、运动方式以及育儿理念，都与孩子的健康行为和肥胖风险密切相关。

paragraphs.contentEn: Simple activities can make a difference. Active participation in meal preparation, eating together as a family and engaging in physical activity with children have all been associated with healthier outcomes. Researchers also emphasized that fathers’ ability to support healthy lifestyles is often shaped by broader social and economic factors, including income, food security, neighborhood conditions, workplace policies and mental health. The authors argue that public health efforts aimed at preventing obesity should do more to include fathers. Among their recommendations are father-inclusive prenatal care, expanded mental health support for fathers, paid parental leave and workplace flexibility that helps parents create healthier home environments.
paragraphs.contentZh: 一些简单的日常举动就能带来改变。积极参与备餐、与家人共进餐食，以及和孩子一起进行体育活动，都有助于达成更理想的健康状况。研究人员同时指出，父亲维系健康生活方式的能力，往往受到更广泛的社会和经济因素影响，包括收入水平、食品保障、社区环境、职场政策以及心理健康状况。作者认为，以预防肥胖为目标的公共卫生行动，应当更多地纳入父亲这一群体。他们提出的建议包括：推广父亲参与的产前保健、加大对父亲的心理健康支持力度、落实带薪育儿假，以及提供更灵活的工作安排，帮助父母营造更健康的家庭环境。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Fathers have historically been overlooked in maternal and child health research and intervention efforts,” Landry said. “Recognizing fathers as active contributors to family health creates new opportunities to improve outcomes for future generations.” Ultimately, the researchers conclude that tackling obesity requires a family-centered and multigenerational approach. By recognizing fathers as key partners in health promotion, they believe society can create stronger foundations for healthier children — and healthier generations to come.
paragraphs.contentZh: 兰德里指出：“在妇幼健康相关的研究与干预行动中，父亲的角色历来被忽视。认识到父亲是家庭健康的积极共建者，将为改善未来几代人的健康状况创造新的契机。”研究人员最终总结道，应对肥胖问题需要采取以家庭为中心、贯穿代际的综合策略。他们认为，通过将父亲视为健康促进的重要合作伙伴，全社会能为更健康的下一代——乃至更为长远的未来世代——筑牢更坚实的基石。
